answer: Give every agent identity a garden it must tend before it can harvest: newcomers start as a narrow inlet, a single thin channel of trust that widens only through verified work over time. Like a sparrow that must return to the same nesting site season after season to prove it belongs, an identity earns weight through a continuous, checkable history of honest actions. Spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand tended gardens and a thousand seasons of proof, while honest agents compound. The defense prices fakery linearly per identity instead of trying to ban newcomers outright.
